review.assessment: The change introduces a skeletal `RingBuffer<T>` struct that holds no actual state, relying solely on a zero-sized `PhantomData` marker to satisfy the type system. All public methods are explicitly stubbed with `unimplemented!()`, meaning the buffer cannot allocate storage, track indices, or store items as specified. Consequently, any attempt to instantiate and use the ring buffer will result in an immediate runtime panic instead of functioning correctly.

findings.actual: Struct contains only `_marker: PhantomData<T>`, which occupies zero memory and cannot store data or track ring positions.
findings.expected: Struct must contain fields for capacity and a backing collection (e.g., `Vec<T>` or array) along with head/tail indices to manage circular wrapping.

findings.actual: Every method body contains `unimplemented!()` and panics immediately upon invocation.
findings.call: Instantiate RingBuffer and invoke any method (e.g., `ring.push(1)` in a test)
findings.defect: All public methods are unimplemented stubs
findings.expected: Methods should manage buffer indices, handle capacity allocation, overwrite oldest elements when full, and return correct lengths/vectors.
